invocation_origin: jswarm.portal example fixture (shipped so the UAT/FIX portal has real data to build against on a fresh clone)
decision: Charter the session-expiry defect for repair; the fix contract below is authorized against it.
summary: Signed-in users are logged out roughly one minute earlier than the session's advertised lifetime.
Root cause: the expiry check compares against server-received time instead of the token's own issued-at claim, so ordinary clock skew between the token issuer and the session host is charged twice.

pm_view.quote: Customers are being signed out mid-task with no warning, and the support queue is filling with 'I just typed my password 5 minutes ago' tickets.

terminal_outcome.statement: A session issued with a given Max-Age lasts that long, regardless of ordinary clock skew between the issuer and the session host.
bullets: The expiry check is anchored to the token's own issued-at claim, not to server receive time.
A skew of up to 5 seconds between issuer and host no longer shortens the effective session.

pm_anchor_map.controlling_sentence: The expiry check anchors to received_at instead of the token's own issued_at claim.
pm_anchor_map.how_it_serves: Names the exact comparison a repair must change, so the fix contract's scope is unambiguous.

in_scope.item: Session expiry calculation in the auth middleware.
in_scope.reason: Direct cause of the reported early logout.

out_of_scope.reason: Not needed to fix the expiry calculation; would widen the change far beyond the reported defect.

defects.conviction: Confirmed by reproduction: a session with Max-Age=3600 issued at T is rejected as expired at T+3540, consistently, across three independent sessions.

flow.body: issue token(issued_at=T, max_age=3600) -> host receives at T+delta -> host computes expiry = received_at + max_age instead of issued_at + max_age -> session appears to expire delta seconds early

risks.risk: Widening the fix to touch token issuance as well as validation could change the token format for other consumers.
risks.impact: Would require a coordinated rollout instead of a single-service fix.
risks.guardrail: Repair authority is scoped to the validation-side expiry calculation only; see out_of_scope_boundaries.

cost_timeline.text: Small, single-file change; verified locally in under a day once charted.

sections.title: Root cause
sections.body: The expiry check anchors to `received_at` (server receive time) instead of the token's own `issued_at` claim, so ordinary clock skew between issuer and host is charged against the user's session lifetime twice: once implicitly at issuance, and again at every validation.

sections.title: Reproduction
sections.body: Issue a session with Max-Age=3600 from a host whose clock reads 60 seconds ahead of the validating host. The session is rejected as expired at T+3540 instead of T+3600, on every request, not intermittently.

uat_route: Sign in, wait until shortly before the advertised session lifetime elapses, and confirm the session is still valid at that point.
vendor_policy: No third-party or vendor code is touched by this defect; the expiry calculation is first-party.

accepted_user_outcome.statement: A user who is told their session lasts an hour gets the full hour, not 59 minutes.

out_of_scope_boundaries.reason: The defect is in validation-side expiry math, not in what the token carries.

probe_constraints.constraint: Any fix must not require re-issuing already-active sessions.

conviction_state.summary: Reproduced deterministically across three sessions with a fixed clock-skew rig; root cause isolated to a single comparison in the expiry check.
